title: M1 — Streaming completion (provider layer)
source: SPECIFICATION.md §4 (provider layer), §3 (data model), §12 (layer drivers). Milestone M1: can perform a one-shot streamed completion against Anthropic. No agent loop, no tools, no harness.

known_failures: No dune-project exists — build cannot run at all
baseline.notes: Reuse audit: nothing exists yet. All modules are new. JSON repair is a port of vendor/pi/packages/ai/src/utils/json-parse.ts repairJson() + parseStreamingJson(). SSE parsing tests are ported from vendor/pi/packages/ai/test/anthropic-sse-parsing.test.ts. JSON schema tests are ported from vendor/pi/packages/ai/test/validation.test.ts. No Pi equivalent exists for the SSE chunk parser (Pi uses the Anthropic SDK internally) or Event_stream (Pi uses JS async generators).

epochs.title: M1 — Provider layer
epochs.description: Build the provider layer from scratch: data model types, JSON schema validator, JSON repair, SSE chunk parser, Anthropic SSE interpreter, Event_stream Eio primitive, Anthropic HTTP module, and provider_driver. At the end of this epoch the provider_driver binary can stream a completion from Anthropic (run manually with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). CI validates everything except the live network call.

stages.title: Project scaffold: dune-project, opam files, CI, formatting
stages.description: Create the dune build system, opam package definitions, GitHub Actions CI workflow, ocamlformat config, and pre-commit hook. Empty libraries that compile to nothing. After this stage dune build succeeds on an empty project.
stages.implementation_notes: dune-project should declare OCaml >= 5.4 and dune >= 3.16. Library names: pera_types, pera_provider. opam files declare dependencies: pera-types needs containers, yojson; pera-provider needs pera-types, containers, yojson, eio, eio_main, eio_linux, piaf, re. The drivers binary depends on pera-provider, eio_main. CI: ocaml/setup-ocaml@v3, pin OCaml 5.4, opam install --deps-only, dune build, dune runtest. Trigger on PRs only. .ocamlformat: use defaults (empty file is valid). pre-commit: run ocamlformat --check on staged .ml/.mli files; exit 1 if any fail. Install via scripts/pre-commit symlinked to .git/hooks/pre-commit — include a note in the script that this must be installed manually (git hooks are not committed). Note: dune-project and opam files must list all deps even though the libraries are empty — this ensures opam install works from the start.

test_requirements.notes: No tests yet. Acceptance is dune build succeeding on an empty but valid project.

stages.title: Core data model types (pera_types)
stages.description: Define all data model types from spec §3 in the pera_types library. Pure types, no IO. These are the vocabulary everything else is built on. .mli first, then .ml.
stages.implementation_notes: Define in types.mli (and implement in types.ml): (1) Content variants: user_content = UText of string | UImage of { url: string; media_type: string }; assistant_content = AText of string | AThinking of { text: string; signature: string option } | AToolCall of tool_call; tool_call = { id: string; name: string; arguments: Yojson.Safe.t }; tool_result_content = { tool_call_id: string; content: Yojson.Safe.t; is_error: bool }. (2) Message types: user_message = { role: string (* 'user' *); content: user_content list }; assistant_message = { content: assistant_content list; stop_reason: stop_reason; provenance: provenance; usage: usage }. (3) stop_reason = EndTurn | ToolUse | MaxTokens | StopSequence | Error | Aborted. (4) usage = { input_tokens: int; output_tokens: int; cache_read_tokens: int; cache_write_tokens: int; cost_usd: float option }. (5) provenance = { api: string; provider: string; model: string; error_message: string option }. (6) assistant_message_event (AME): type assistant_message_event = AME_text_start of { partial: assistant_message } | AME_text_delta of { text: string; partial: assistant_message } | AME_thinking_start of { partial: assistant_message } | AME_thinking_delta of { text: string; partial: assistant_message } | AME_tool_call_start of { index: int; id: string; name: string; partial: assistant_message } | AME_tool_call_delta of { index: int; arguments_fragment: string; partial: assistant_message } | AME_tool_call_end of { index: int; partial: assistant_message } | AME_done of { message: assistant_message } | AME_error of { message: string; partial: assistant_message }. The partial field in each event is an immutable snapshot of the assistant_message as it stands — see spec §4 'Partial messages'. (7) Error families: file_error_code = NotFound | PermissionDenied | Timeout | Aborted | Unknown; file_error = { code: file_error_code; path: string; message: string }; execution_error_code = Timeout | Aborted | NonZeroExit | Unknown; execution_error = { code: execution_error_code; message: string }; tool_error = { message: string; is_user_error: bool }. (8) model = { id: string; api: string (* 'anthropic' | 'openai-completions' *) }. All types: open Containers at top of .ml. No structural equality.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: module-boundaries.md — .mli first, abstract types where appropriate
type-safety.md — variants over strings for stop_reason, error codes
pera-specific.md — open Containers, no structural equality

stages.title: JSON schema validator (pera_provider)
stages.description: Implement the runtime JSON schema type and validator used for tool argument schemas (spec §9). Standalone module, no dependency on pera_types. Tests ported from Pi's validation.test.ts.
stages.implementation_notes: Implement the schema DSL from spec §9: constructors object, string, number, integer, boolean, array, optional, enum, const, any_of. Each takes optional metadata (description, constraints). Two functions on schema values: (1) to_json : t -> Yojson.Safe.t — renders to JSON Schema draft-07 for sending to the LLM. (2) validate : t -> Yojson.Safe.t -> (unit, string) result — validates an argument value. Validation must handle type coercion as Pi does (string '42' -> integer 42, 'true' -> boolean, etc.) because Anthropic sometimes sends tool arguments as JSON strings wrapping the actual value. See vendor/pi/packages/ai/test/validation.test.ts for the 14 coercion cases and 4 rejection cases to replicate. Do NOT use GADTs or ppx — schema is a runtime data value (spec §9 explicitly says this). The type t is a variant; keep it simple.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: error-handling.md — validate returns Result, never raises
partial-functions.md — no Yojson.Util.to_string etc, use _opt variants
type-safety.md — schema type is a closed variant, not strings

stages.title: JSON repair (pera_provider)
stages.description: Port Pi's repairJson and parseStreamingJson to OCaml. Handles the malformed JSON that Anthropic sends in tool-input deltas: invalid escape sequences (\H) and raw control characters (literal tabs). See vendor/pi/packages/ai/src/utils/json-parse.ts. Tests ported from Pi's anthropic-sse-parsing.test.ts.
stages.implementation_notes: Two functions. (1) repair : string -> string — scans the string and fixes: (a) raw control characters inside JSON strings (tab 0x09, newline 0x0A, carriage return 0x0D etc.) replaced with their escape sequences (\t, \n, \r); (b) invalid backslash escapes (\H, \j, etc. — anything not in the JSON spec set \" \\ \/ \b \f \n \r \t \uXXXX) doubled to \\ so they become a literal backslash. Handle unicode escapes (\uXXXX) correctly — do not double those. See Pi's repairJson implementation. (2) parse_streaming : string option -> (Yojson.Safe.t, string) result — attempt Yojson.Safe.from_string; if that fails, try repair then parse again; return Error if both fail. This is simpler than Pi's version (we skip the partial-json tier since OCaml does not have an equivalent library and concatenation-at-block-stop handles the incompleteness case). Reference: vendor/pi/packages/ai/src/utils/json-parse.ts lines 32-124.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: error-handling.md — parse_streaming returns Result
pattern-matching.md — match on Bytes/char ranges for the repair scanner
pera-specific.md — open Containers

stages.title: SSE chunk parser (pera_provider)
stages.description: Implement the provider-agnostic SSE chunk parser (spec §4 'SSE parsing — two layers', Layer A). Byte chunks in, framed events out. Pure function over strings, no Eio. No Pi equivalent — Pi uses the Anthropic SDK for this layer.
stages.implementation_notes: Define: type framed_event = { event_type: string; data: string; id: string option }. type state (opaque, holds partial line buffer). val initial_state : state. val feed : state -> string -> state * framed_event list. The feed function processes a chunk: append to buffer, scan for complete events (\n\n delimiter between fields). Each event is delimited by a blank line. Fields: 'event:', 'data:', 'id:'. Multi-line data: fields with the same key have their values joined with newlines. 'data:' fields with no value (just 'data:') produce empty string. Incomplete events (chunk ends mid-field) stay in the buffer for the next call. Do not depend on pera_types — this is a pure byte-level parser. Reference: spec §4 'SSE — what's on the wire'. Use QCheck for property tests on chunk boundary splitting.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: pattern-matching.md — match on string structure for field parsing
naming-and-intermediates.md — name intermediate parse steps clearly
pera-specific.md — open Containers

new_tests.description: A complete SSE event in a single chunk produces one framed_event.
An event split at a byte boundary across two feed calls produces one event on the second call.

new_tests.description: Two complete SSE events in one chunk produce two framed_events.
new_tests.asserts: feed produces a list of length 2 with correct event_type for each

new_tests.description: An SSE event with only a data field (no event: line) has event_type = ''.

new_tests.description: QCheck: for any valid SSE byte sequence, splitting it at a random byte boundary and feeding in two chunks produces the same events as feeding the whole sequence in one chunk.

stages.title: Anthropic SSE interpreter (pera_provider)
stages.description: Implement the Anthropic-specific SSE interpreter (spec §4 'SSE parsing — two layers', Layer B). State machine consuming framed_events, emitting assistant_message_events with immutable partial snapshots. Uses pera_types and json_repair. Tests ported from Pi's anthropic-sse-parsing.test.ts.
stages.implementation_notes: Define: type state (internal; holds in-progress assistant_message builder — completed blocks, active text/thinking buffer, active tool call buffer, accumulated usage). val initial_state : state. val feed : state -> framed_event -> state * assistant_message_event list. The interpreter handles Anthropic's SSE event lifecycle: message_start initialises state; content_block_start begins a text, thinking, or tool_use block; content_block_delta appends to the active block (text_delta for text/thinking, input_json_delta for tool_use — concatenate raw fragment strings, do not parse yet); content_block_stop finalises the block (for tool_use: call json_repair.parse_streaming on the concatenated input_json); message_delta updates stop_reason and usage; message_stop emits AME_done. Each emission carries an immutable assistant_message snapshot built from current builder state — see spec §4 'Partial messages — the snapshot decision'. Unknown event types (e.g. 'done', 'proxy.stats', 'ping') are silently ignored. Reference: vendor/pi/packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts lines 256-353 and vendor/pi/packages/ai/test/anthropic-sse-parsing.test.ts.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: pattern-matching.md — exhaustive match on known event types; unknown goes to catch-all (open type — one of the rare legitimate catch-all cases)
error-handling.md — json_repair failures produce AME_error, never raise
pera-specific.md — open Containers, immutable snapshots

stages.title: Event_stream Eio primitive (pera_provider)
stages.description: Implement the generic ('event, 'result) Event_stream.t over Eio.Stream.t + Eio.Promise.t (spec §4 'The event stream primitive'). Used at three levels of the stack; this stage builds the shared primitive.
stages.implementation_notes: type ('event, 'result) t = { stream: 'event Eio.Stream.t; result: ('result, string) result Eio.Promise.t * ('result, string) result Eio.Promise.u }. Expose: val create : capacity:int -> ('e, 'r) t * (('e, 'r) t -> unit) — returns stream and a push function. val push : ('e, 'r) t -> 'e -> unit. val close : ('e, 'r) t -> 'r -> unit — resolves the promise with Ok. val close_error : ('e, 'r) t -> string -> unit — resolves with Error. val take : ('e, 'r) t -> [ `Event of 'e | `Done of 'r | `Error of string ] — takes one event or the resolved result. val iter : ('e, 'r) t -> f:('e -> unit) -> ('r, string) result — consume all events. val result : ('e, 'r) t -> ('r, string) result — await promise (blocks). Default capacity: 32 (spec says bounded). A stalled consumer will backpressure the producer through Eio.Stream.add which blocks when full. Tests use Eio_main.run and Eio.Fiber.fork_seq.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: pera-specific.md §5 — Eio conventions: fibres under switch, Eio.Cancel not flags
error-handling.md — close_error takes string; callers convert to typed errors at their layer
module-boundaries.md — .mli hides the internal Eio.Stream.t and Promise.t

new_tests.description: One fibre pushes 3 events and closes; the main fibre collects via iter. Verify all 3 events arrive and result is Ok.

new_tests.description: Producer calls close_error; consumer's iter returns Error.
new_tests.asserts: iter returns Error message matching close_error argument

new_tests.description: Create stream with capacity 1. Producer pushes 2 events without yielding. Verify the second push blocks until the consumer takes the first.
new_tests.asserts: Producer is blocked; after consumer takes first event, second event is deliverable

stages.title: Anthropic HTTP module + provider_driver (pera_provider + bin/drivers)
stages.description: Wire piaf to the SSE interpreter via Event_stream to produce a working Anthropic provider. Define the Provider.S module type. Build provider_driver as a manual validation binary. This is the M1 acceptance proof — run manually with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to confirm the milestone.
stages.implementation_notes: Define Provider.S in provider.mli (spec §4 'Provider interface'): module type S = sig val name : string; val stream_simple : model:model -> context:context -> options:simple_stream_options -> sw:Eio.Switch.t -> (assistant_message_event, assistant_message) Event_stream.t end. Define context = { system: string; messages: message list; tools: tool_schema list; thinking: bool } and simple_stream_options = { max_tokens: int; temperature: float option }. message = UserMessage of user_message | AssistantMessage of assistant_message. Implement Anthropic_provider satisfying Provider.S: use piaf to POST to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages with Accept: text/event-stream. Pipe response body bytes through Sse_parser.feed then Anthropic_interpreter.feed, pushing assistant_message_events into the Event_stream. Close the stream with the final assistant_message from AME_done or AME_error. Auth: read API key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var (or accept as argument). provider_driver.ml: parse argv (model, prompt text). Construct a minimal context. Call Anthropic_provider.stream_simple. Print each event as it arrives (event type + truncated content). Print final message on AME_done. Exit 1 on AME_error. Gracefully skip if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set (print 'skipped: no API key' and exit 0). The driver is NOT included in dune runtest — it is a manual tool. Exclude from CI via (enabled_if (env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)) or by not adding it to any runtest alias.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: pera-specific.md §5 — Eio: fibres under switch, sw passed as labelled arg
pera-specific.md §6 — IO returns Result, never raises
module-boundaries.md — Provider.S is the public seam; hide piaf internals in anthropic_provider.ml

test_requirements.notes: No automated tests for this stage — the driver requires a live Anthropic API key and is intentionally excluded from dune runtest. The acceptance criterion is the driver binary building and running successfully against the API. The test-reviewer should flag this as an acknowledged exception (network-dependent live API), not a missing test.
